solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Marshal nominates 1 in 50

definitions.note: one of the fifty United States

indicators.note: to marshal is to arrange or put in order, so the letters of the next word are lined up afresh

explanation.surface: A US marshal puts forward someone for office in one of the fifty states.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Marshal' reads as a lawman's title, but it is the verb to arrange, rearranging NOMINATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Minnesota is one of the fifty states of the USA, so it is literally one state in fifty.

clue.text: Got married without the Church — married still

indicators.note: without tells us to take away the letters for the church from the longer word

parts.note: to get matched is to be paired off as a couple, so got married gives matched
CH is the standard abbreviation for church

explanation.surface: A couple wed in a civil ceremony rather than in church, and are still together.
explanation.walkthrough: 'still' signals that the shortened word still means married: MATCHED loses CH but keeps the sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Mated means paired or joined as partners, a looser synonym for wedded.

clue.text: Some newspapers for citizens

definitions.meaning: newspapers sold across the whole country, as opposed to local papers
people who belong to a country

explanation.surface: Certain papers are written for the people of a country.
explanation.definitionFit: Britain's nationwide papers are called the nationals; a national is also a citizen of a state.

clue.text: It releases unusually bitter blows

indicators.note: unusually means in an unusual arrangement, so the letters of the two words are reordered

explanation.surface: Something lets loose unexpectedly harsh gusts of wind.
explanation.walkthrough: 'blows' looks like strikes, but here it is a noun for winds; 'unusually' rearranges IT RELEASES.
explanation.definitionFit: Winds from the east bring cold continental air to Britain, so easterly gales are often bitterly cold.

clue.text: Work associated with a financial centre lacks transparency

definitions.note: the clue phrase describes having the quality; the answer is the noun for that quality, the lack of clarity

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work in music
the City is London's financial district

explanation.surface: A deal involving a banking district is not open and clear.
explanation.walkthrough: The City is the square mile of London that houses its banks and markets.
explanation.definitionFit: Opacity is the state of being opaque, letting no light through, hence lacking openness or clarity.

clue.text: Yorkshire headwear appropriate on the line

parts.note: Yorkshire speakers drop the H, so hats becomes 'ats
to appropriate is to take for yourself

explanation.surface: A Yorkshireman's hat is suitable for wearing while on the telephone.
explanation.walkthrough: Dropping initial H is a stereotype of Yorkshire and other northern English accents; 'appropriate' is the verb, not the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Something on the line is at risk, the same idiom as being staked in a wager.

clue.text: Uneven parts of barley and wheat produce

indicators.note: uneven means odd-numbered, so take the first, third, fifth letters and so on

explanation.surface: Patchy bits of the grain crops are what a farm harvests.
explanation.definitionFit: Bread is the food made from wheat flour, one of the main products of the crop.

clue.text: Fish out of river may be a ray

indicators.note: out of tells us the river letter leaves the fish word

parts.note: the bream is a freshwater fish

explanation.surface: A fish taken from the river might turn out to be a ray.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ray' looks like another fish, but it means a beam of light.
explanation.definitionFit: A beam of light and a ray of light are the same thing, a narrow shaft.

clue.text: Unseen nuisance that's a source of tedium

indicators.note: the letters are drawn from inside the two words, which are their source

explanation.surface: An invisible annoyance is what makes life boring.
explanation.definitionFit: Ennui is a French loan word for listless boredom.

clue.text: Black Bess, for example, reveals unexpected talent

definitions.meaning: Black Bess was the black mare of the highwayman Dick Turpin, a horse of dark colour
a little-known competitor who turns out surprisingly able

explanation.surface: A famous horse turns out to have hidden abilities.
explanation.walkthrough: Dick Turpin was an 18th-century English highwayman; legend gives him the mare Black Bess.
explanation.definitionFit: Literally a horse of dark colour, and idiomatically a person whose abilities come as a surprise.

clue.text: Oddly it's out east he plotted conspiracy

indicators.note: oddly means in an odd way, so the letters of the phrase are put in a strange new order

explanation.surface: Strangely, word has leaked to the east about who hatched the plot.
explanation.walkthrough: Titus Oates invented the 'Popish Plot' of 1678, a fictitious Catholic conspiracy to kill Charles II.
explanation.definitionFit: This English fabricator concocted a supposed Catholic plan against the king.

clue.text: Party-pooper, in more ways than one!

definitions.text: Party-pooper, in more ways than one!

parts.words: Party-pooper, in more ways than one!
parts.note: someone who refuses drink spoils the fun at a party, and someone who refuses to vote lets down a political party

explanation.surface: A killjoy who spoils things in several ways.
explanation.definitionFit: One who abstains may decline alcohol at a celebration or decline to cast a vote for a political party.

clue.text: You need 12 to form such a system

definitions.text: You need 12 to form such a system

parts.words: You need 12 to form such a system
parts.note: a counting system based on twelve, with twelve digits

explanation.surface: A dozen of something are required to build a system.
explanation.definitionFit: A base-twelve number system uses twelve digits, so twelve symbols are needed to write it.

clue.text: Old friends like Christopher and Elspeth at the end

parts.note: Kit is a short form of the name Christopher

indicators.note: at the end points to the last letter of the name Elspeth

explanation.surface: A pair of long-standing pals named Christopher and Elspeth turn up at the finish.
explanation.definitionFit: Kith is an old word for one's friends and acquaintances, as in kith and kin.

clue.text: Hitchcock's outstanding feature?

parts.note: the film director's jowly profile, a feature that literally stands out from his face

explanation.surface: Which is Alfred Hitchcock's best film?
explanation.definitionFit: Alfred Hitchcock's famous silhouette shows heavy jowls, a fold of flesh that protrudes under the jaw.

clue.text: Cook taking tail off displays weakness

indicators.note: the cooking word takes in the other letters, holding them inside

parts.note: to fry is to cook in fat

indicators.note: off means gone wrong, so the letters of tail are scrambled

explanation.surface: A chef removes the tail from a fish before serving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'taking tail off' reads as cutting a tail away, but 'off' is the anagram signal for TAIL and 'taking' is the container.
explanation.definitionFit: Frailty is the quality of being feeble or easily broken, a synonym for weakness.

clue.text: Having spelt "safe" wrong could put you in danger

definitions.note: the clue phrase describes what a misstep does; the answer is the noun for such a slip

indicators.note: spelling something wrong puts its letters out of order, so they are rearranged

explanation.surface: Misspelling the word safe could ironically leave you in peril.
explanation.definitionFit: A misstep, literal or figurative, is a blunder that can lead to harm or trouble.

clue.text: Defaced weapon naturally changes with time

definitions.note: the clue phrase is a verb phrase; the answer is the noun for something that does this

indicators.note: defaced means its face, the front letter, is removed

parts.note: a revolver is a handgun

explanation.surface: A disfigured gun is something that alters gradually over the years.
explanation.definitionFit: Something that evolves develops gradually by natural processes, as species do over generations.

clue.text: Hesitate to get sick during leave

indicators.note: during places the sickness word in the midst of the leaving word

parts.note: to vacate is to leave a place
ill means sick

explanation.surface: Someone holds back from falling ill while on holiday.
explanation.walkthrough: 'leave' looks like a noun, time off work, but it is the verb VACATE.
explanation.definitionFit: To vacillate is to waver between options, unable to decide.

clue.text: Cuts classes in oral comprehension

indicators.note: comprehending something spoken means understanding it by ear, so we go by how the word sounds

parts.note: lessons are classes at school

explanation.surface: A school drops sessions in its spoken-understanding course.
explanation.definitionFit: To lessen something is to reduce it, as a cut in spending reduces it.

clue.text: Unfit editors may need such injections

definitions.note: the clue speaks of the jabs in the plural; the answer is one drug of that kind

indicators.note: unfit means not in proper shape, so the letters are put into a new shape

explanation.surface: Out-of-shape journalists may need performance-boosting jabs.
explanation.definitionFit: Steroids are hormone drugs often given by injection, for medicine or illicit body-building.

clue.text: ABCDE confused the French — what a fiasco!

indicators.note: confused means muddled, so the five letters are put in a different order

parts.note: le is the French masculine word for the

explanation.surface: The French were baffled by the alphabet's opening letters, a complete disaster.
explanation.definitionFit: A debacle is a sudden humiliating collapse or utter failure.

clue.text: This red mixture does 16

definitions.note: 16 down is the verb hesitate, so doing it means wavering

indicators.note: a mixture of the letters means they are stirred into a new order

explanation.surface: This red blend behaves in some numbered way.
explanation.definitionFit: To dither is to be indecisive, the same as wavering or hesitating.

clue.text: A divine youth's painful setback

indicators.note: set back means put backwards, so the painful word is read in reverse

parts.note: sore means painful

explanation.surface: A godlike young man suffers a hurtful reverse.
explanation.definitionFit: Eros is the Greek god of love, usually pictured as a winged boy or young man.

clue.text: See 9
A commercial success: what oenophiles long for, we're told

indicators.note: being told something means hearing it, so we go by sound

parts.note: wine lovers long for the finest wine store, the best cellar

explanation.surface: A hit product is what wine buffs crave.
explanation.walkthrough: An oenophile is a wine connoisseur, who would covet a superb wine store.
explanation.definitionFit: A book or product that sells in huge numbers is a top seller.

clue.text: Have another go at 24

parts.note: 24 down is an exam, and to take an exam again after failing is this

explanation.surface: Try once more at the clue numbered twenty-four.
explanation.walkthrough: In Britain, a student who fails an exam usually has the chance to sit it a second time.
explanation.definitionFit: To sit an examination again is the British term for retaking it.

clue.text: Contestant takes part in experiment

indicators.note: the word gives up part of itself, a stretch of its letters

explanation.surface: A competitor participates in a scientific trial.
explanation.walkthrough: 'takes part' reads as joining in, but it means a section of CONTESTANT supplies the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A test is a trial or experiment carried out to find something out.

clue.text: Crazy little hero, beheaded in Peter Pan, say

indicators.note: crazy means mad or disordered, so the gathered letters are rearranged
beheaded means the word loses its head, its first letter

explanation.surface: A mad little hero loses his head in the story of the boy who never grew up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beheaded' removes the H of HERO to give ERO; 'Crazy' rearranges LITTLE plus ERO.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Pan is the character the play is named after, the lead whose name is the title.

clue.text: Very many are out of shape

indicators.note: out of shape tells us the word is bent out of its usual form, so its letters are reshuffled

explanation.surface: Lots of people are not physically fit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of shape' reads as unfit, but 'out of' is the anagram signal and SHAPE the fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Heaps is informal for a great number or a lot, as in heaps of time.

clue.text: Assume, for argument's sake, it follows return of bribe

indicators.note: follows puts it after the reversed bribe word
a return sends the bribe word back the way it came, so it reads backwards

parts.note: a sop is something given to pacify or bribe someone

explanation.surface: Suppose, for the sake of debate, that something comes after a pay-off is returned.
explanation.definitionFit: To posit is to put forward a proposition as a basis for argument.

clue.text: Debug beds in Homes and Gardens

definitions.text: Debug beds in Homes and Gardens

parts.words: Debug beds in Homes and Gardens
parts.note: both bedrooms and flower beds can harbour bugs, which must be cleaned away

explanation.surface: A magazine feature on ridding beds of pests.
explanation.walkthrough: Homes and Gardens is a British home-interest magazine; the beds are both sleeping beds and garden plots.
explanation.definitionFit: To rid something of germs or bugs is to cleanse it with chemicals.
